ICS: Open the interview (greet the patient, make introductions, negotiate an agenda for this follow-up visit with the patient).
Build a relationship and establish rapport with patient.
Engage in open-ended inquiry, listening, summarizing.
Assess the patient’s understanding of why she needs a pelvic exam and Pap smear.
Provide appropriate education using patient education techniques.
Explore Mrs. Henderson’s misunderstandings and resistance to having a pelvic exam.
The patient has many concerns and questions about the pap smear.  Explore the patient’s concerns.  What are her reservations?  What alternatives would she find acceptable?
Use techniques learned in lecture and small group.  Practice examples of “ask-teach-ask”, “teach back” or “show me”, and “looking ahead” techniques.
You must understand everything the student tells you, and the student should ask you to repeat things that s/he says or have you describe it in your own words.
If the student is pleasant and convinces you to have a Pap smear without using excessive medical jargon, you agree to do it.
